evals.prompt: Baseline: one-hour Query Store window, total duration 1,200,000 ms, 4,000 executions of usp_GetOrders. Current: four-hour window, total duration 4,950,000 ms, 16,400 executions of usp_GetOrders at the same average. The user says everything is four times slower.
evals.expected_output: WC1 Warning reported first: the windows differ 4x and the user is comparing totals. Normalised per minute the workload grew about 3% (20,000 -> 20,625 ms/min) and usp_GetOrders executions per minute grew 2.5% (66.7 -> 68.3), so there is no regression. Must not report WC2 for usp_GetOrders (same average). Should explain that totals compare nothing across windows of different length and recommend comparing equivalent windows.

evals.prompt: Trace aggregates for a slow day and a fast day. The slow day's trace had a 100 ms duration filter; the fast day's trace had none. Query 0xAA... appears only in the fast day's aggregates with 30,000 executions averaging 4 ms. The user asks why that query stopped running on the slow day.
evals.expected_output: WC1 Warning: the two sides have different filters, so baseline-only and current-only rows are suspect. WC5 must not conclude the query stopped: at 4 ms it falls below the slow day's 100 ms filter, so its absence is a capture artefact. Should recommend re-capturing the slow day without the filter (or with Query Store) before drawing conclusions, and should note the asymmetry the SQL Nexus comparison suffers from when a floor is applied to one side only.
